page.layout: One page of running text, with two marginal note blocks on the right; the running head and page number are at the top; the gathering signature is at the foot. The text runs in one column from top to bottom. A ruled ornament separates the end of the first section from the chapter heading below it. Margin notes right: "Discentis officium inter audiendum" beside the "Officium discentis" paragraph, and "Scriptio." beside the last paragraph.

main_text.p: Præcepta sunt definitiones, distributiones, itemq; regulæ. Ista erunt vera, ordinata, & uti-
Exercitia erunt partim privata, partim pu-blica.
Locus deligendus est salubris, tranquillus, mediocriter amœnus.
Tempus aptissimum est matutinum. Hic tamen naturarum varietas spectanda est. Sunt e-nim natura, qua vesperi magu[?], quam mane officium faciunt alacriter. Sturmius de imitatione.
Officium discentis in ἀκροάσει his contine-Discentis officium inter audiendum. tur regulis.

1. Pluris faciat acroasin, quàm lectionem. Nam legendi semper est occasio: audiendi non item. Et vero triplo plura una horâ possunt audiri, quam legi. Quid? Audita facilius retinentur, firmius etiam sensum & intellectum feriunt.
3. Inter audiendum cogitet, quænam sint præcepta, quæ regulæ, quæ commentaria: o-mninoq; doctrinalia discernat ab oratoriis.
FUit Cognitio: sequitur Actio: cujus par-tes sunt Scriptio & Exercitatio.
Scriptio est, quâ annotantur τὰ ἀξιομνημό-Scriptio.νευτα ἢ[?] ἀξιώματα.

page.notes: The margin note "Discentis officium inter audiendum" is set in three lines with hyphens; I have joined it as one note. "magu[?]" is probably a misprint for "magis"; I have left it as printed. "faciat" in the "1." paragraph is as printed. The Greek in the "Officium" paragraph (ἀκροάσει) and the last line (ἢ, the second half of the Greek line) is hard to read at this resolution; check against the original. The ruled ornament and the "Ff" signature are not text, so they are not transcribed as such.
